provenance.sourcePrompt:
Three-column time-echo split effect over backgroundVideo. Default: full-width single video playing normally. Five times during the clip, the frame splits into three equal vertical columns showing the same video at three time offsets. The split EXITS only when a scene cut is detected in the video — not on a fixed timer
SPLIT ENTER — 5 fixed trigger times
t=2.0s, t=7.0s, t=13.0s, t=19.0s, t=25.5s
Enter animation: 0.15s easeOut. Two black bars (10px wide) slide in simultaneously — left bar from translateX(-100%) to rest at 33.33%, right bar from translateX(+100%) to rest at 66.67%. The split layer (#splitLayer) fades in opacity 0→1 over 0.15s. The full-width single video fades out opacity 1→0 over 0.15s
SPLIT HOLD — time-echo columns
Three absolutely-positioned column wrappers inside #splitLayer, each overflow:hidden, 33.33% wide
Left col (0–33.33%): video element playing backgroundVideo, currentTime = masterTime
Center col (33.33–66.67%): separate video element same src, currentTime = masterTime + 0.3s
Right col (66.67–100%): separate video element same src, currentTime = masterTime + 0.6s
Each video element is 100% container width, object-fit:fill, positioned so only its column's slice is visible. Sync center and right currentTime on every requestAnimationFrame tick. All video elements muted
SCENE-CUT DETECTION for EXIT
Use a hidden offscreen canvas (e.g. 64×36px, sampling the left video)
Every requestAnimationFrame while the split is active
1. Draw the current left video frame onto the canvas
2. Read pixel data with getImageData
3. Compute average luminance of this frame
4. Compare to previous frame's average luminance
5. If the absolute difference in average luminance exceeds threshold (use 18 out of 255 as default), declare a scene cut
6. On scene cut detected: immediately begin EXIT animation
Also EXIT if the split has been held for more than 4.0 seconds (safety fallback) with no cut detected
SPLIT EXIT — triggered by scene cut OR 4s fallback
Exit animation: 0.15s easeIn
The ENTIRE #splitLayer exits as one atomic unit — apply a single CSS transition on #splitLayer: opacity 1→0 over 0.15s. No per-column stagger
Simultaneously: left bar translateX(0)→translateX(-100%), right bar translateX(0)→translateX(+100%), both 0.15s easeIn
Full-width single video fades back in: opacity 0→1 over 0.15s
After exit completes, disable detection loop until next enter trigger
BETWEEN EVENTS
#splitLayer visibility:hidden and opacity:0. Full-width video opacity:1. No artifacts
DIVIDER BARS (inside #splitLayer, inherit parent opacity on exit)
Two divs, 10px wide, 100% height, background:#000, box-shadow:0 0 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.45)
Left bar: position:absolute, left:calc(33.33% - 5px). Right bar: left:calc(66.67% - 5px)
z-index above column videos
No text, no captions, no icons, no UI elements of any kind. Pure geometric temporal split on a serene matte pastel ancient Chinese landscape
